issue: Under the physical restraint enhancement in U.S.S.G. § 2B3.1(b)(4)(B), must the restraint be sustained or last for some minimum duration, or can a brief restraint, such as ordering a victim to the floor, suffice?

sides.position: Restraint must show a 'sustained focus' on the victim, and a brief restraint lasting only seconds does not qualify (the narrow view).
cases: United States v. Bell, 947 F.3d 49 (3d Cir. 2020)

sides.position: Brief restraint can satisfy the sustained-focus standard, so a short order to lie down or sit on the floor supports the enhancement.
cases: United States v. Coleman, 664 F.3d 1047 (6th Cir. 2012)

this_court: The majority adopted the narrow Ninth Circuit view and held the enhancement inapplicable because there was no sustained focus on the victim. The dissent would have applied the enhancement.
quote: Although I refrain from commenting on the propriety of adopting this factor — that is, whether the majority was correct to adopt the narrow view of the Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit in the circuit split on this issue — I believe that Bell's conduct also satisfies this factor.
cite: United States v. Marquise Bell, 947 F.3d 49 (3rd Cir. 2020)
